Name: Elijah Williamson
Question: What things do people say that make you roll your eyes?
Answer: A guy from my neighbourhood came to my house some time ago asking for help. He had gotten a flat tire and wanted to borrow my spare for the following day as he needed to check out a job in the morning. From the moment we started speaking to the moment we parted, our conversation was a series of eye rolling on my part. Me: So how come you don't have a spare? Him: I just bought an amp and some speakers. Money’s finished. My car probably has the best music setup in the whole street. Me: (At his house) But look you have another car here. Why don't you use this car? Him: That car isn't working. Me: Then why don't you use one of the tires. It's the same size. Him: That's not my car that's my wife's. Wife (comes out to say hello, seemingly drunk): I have a car for sale. If you only see the engine on this car. Proceeds to open the hood on the car previously mentioned. Me: But is this car working? Wife: Who says it's not working? (glares at husband). Me: (Looking at the engine) Why are there sunflower seeds on top the carburetor? Wife: That damn parrot! It acts as if this car is his house. Husband: I'm actually a mechanic myself. Me: (Tempted to say ‘But you can't fix your wife's car?’) Mmhmm. Husband: I have practically every tool there are for cars. Me: (Tempted to say ‘But you don't have a spare tire.’) Mmhmm Husband: If ever you need work done on your car be sure to check me. Me: Will do. Husband: Can I borrow your tire wrench? I can't find mine. Husband: I can do masonry, plumbing, electrical, roofing. Wife: He's very talented. I never have to call anybody to get work done. I have an entire contracting company living in my house. Husband: Take my number. (He proceeds to search for a call card in his wallet but the area is in darkness.) Honey shine a light on my wallet for a second. Me: Why don't you put up some lights in the front yard? Husband: (Says nothing) Wife: (Scowling) The man just asked you a question. Husband: Well your spare didn't fit but thanks for the help anyway. Me: No problem. Husband: Can you do me one more favour? Me: (groaning) What? Husband: (Whispering so his wife, who went back in the house, doesn't hear). Can you lend me $20? I’ll need it for gas in the morning. Me: Sure (hands him a $20) Husband: (whispering even softer) You want a beer? Me: Yeah why not. Husband: If I go with you she'll know that I'm going for alcohol. You don't mind going to the grocery and getting it for us. (Hands me back my $20) Me: (Puts $20 back in wallet). Sure thing man. I then went home. I wonder how long he waited until it dawned on him that I was not coming back with his beers.

Name: Elijah Williamson
Question: What advice changed your life financially?
Answer: Observing people’s lives rather than listening to their advice is what inspired my spending habits. So many people who draw some sort of salary have advice about spending that money. Spending advice is at every corner I turn. Here are some examples of such advice I encountered : I get that sort of advice practically everywhere, whether it be my co-workers, acquaintances and within my family, everybody is willing to guide me on how to save a couple bucks here and there with their helpful hints. But one thing that I can never discuss with them is this one taboo question, 'Are you satisfied with the direction of your life?’ Such a question would be considered condescending so such conversation is avoided. I look at the person giving me advice and ask myself does he/she lead the kind of life I want. Do I really want to be that guy stuck in a unfulfilling job to ensure that I pay off my car loan, coming home to an apartment to eat a can of Goya beans every evening? I've met so many people who base their lives around simple analogies: ‘You’re only young once.’ ‘Life is short.’ ‘You can’t eat money.’ ‘Treat yourself.’ ‘Work hard, play hard.’ Regardless of their responsibilities and obligations in life these are their core beliefs and they believe they have the wisdom to offer advice to all listening ears based on their beloved ambiguous three word quotes. In my view this is just a convenient mindset in which one can deny accountability for one self. ‘Honey I'm sorry but I can't pay rent this month. I was hanging out with the boys and one thing leads to another. Life is short. Can you borrow some more money from your parents?’ ‘No I'm not selling my car. This is a limited edition. I'll pay you back what I borrowed before the year is over. Life is short and you can't eat money.’ Sad to say these are the same kind if individuals who are most vocal when it comes to giving advice, personal and financial. If someone's personal lifestyle does not agree with you then do not follow their financial advice. One always goes with the other. In a nutshell I would advise that you stop listening to financial advice from those who place more value on emotional satisfaction. Just my 2¢. A donkey can bray as loud and as often as it feels to but it can never convince anyone that it is a horse.

Name: Elijah Williamson
Question: Have you ever sabotaged food because someone was stealing it?
Answer: Is it possible to sabotage someone's lunch by accident? Yes it is. I was the saboteur. The idiot saboteur. Summer was a co-worker of mine at a warehouse I was employed in during my early adulthood. She was a nice girl but she would often get entangled in workplace drama with other provocative and emotional females likes herself. Things got so bad with her that her enemies would go to extreme lengths to sully her reputation or cause harm e.g. calling her boyfriend at night using a private number, spread nasty rumors (some turned out to be true) about her amongst her closest workmates. To work in such an environment could make any girl a little paranoid. Summer was no exception. One faithful afternoon I was about to enjoy my lunch in our staff lunch room. Lunch times were staggered at 12–1pm for some 1–2pm for the rest. I would normally take my lunch at 12pm while Summer took hers afterwards at 1pm. I collected my lunch in the staff fridge and heated it in the microwave. I joined my friends in the 'mess hall’ where we proceeded to have a very exciting conversation about what crap to do with our money when we got paid. While tearing into a chicken drumstick someone made a comment that my mother prepared a really nice lunch for me today. I took a good look down at my lunch bowl and my heart sank. This wasn't my lunch! It was the exact same bowl like mine…..with an orange cover, a little better kept though…..but this was someone else's lunch! I tried to keep my cool. I told my friends I needed to reheat my lunch. Scared to death I would chance upon the true owner coming towards the kitchen, spotting me carrying his/her lunch like a bloody beggar-thief I haphazardly threw the lunch back into the fridge and took out mine. I heated it and returned to my friends like a nervous wreck but eliciting no suspicions. An hour later I'm busy at work when a stern voice comes over the loudspeaker. 'Will all members of staff please report to the kitchen area?’ My heart leaped like stallion in heat. This is it. The s**t has hit the fan. My friends ambled towards me all curious-like saying stuff like 'What the hell is this about?’ and 'Hey, you saw Summer come out from the manager's office in tears? What's her problem now?’ I tried to play it cool but did a terrible job. 'Huh? What da f**k's going on? I got an order to finish. This is bulls**t. Summer is a ho.’ It's a wonder none of them suspected me right then and there. For all staff to be called to a meeting at once meant that this was pretty serious. Somebody's gonna get sent home. My hands started trembling. The warehouse director took center stage and with a wary look on her face explained that Summer had just gone to have her lunch when she observed that it was severely tampered with. She explained that the person tampered with the lunch in such an extreme manner as if to send an insulting, threatening message to her. The director asked that whomsoever did such an act to please reveal him/herself. All the while I stood looking like this: While everyone else around me started to giggle quietly. Summer who stood next to the director stared at me and I immediately looked away. No one came forward. The director gave Summer money to buy lunch. Case dismissed. As we headed back to our respective positions my friends made light banter about the situation. 'We have a food molester at the warehouse. Anyone of us could be the dreaded food molester.’ They then began to laugh. That became a running joke in the warehouse. Twenty minutes later Summer comes towards me and I start to quiver like jelly. 'You see anybody with an orange cover bowl when you were at lunch Elijah?’ I shook my head in the negative. 'Sick f**king people we have working here,’ she continued. 'Yeah.' I said flatly, 'Hmmm.’ 'I mean,’ she continued while raising her voice, 'Interfering with my food? If that person has a problem with me I don't care what they say to my face but to know that some nasty sonofab**ch will go so low…….I mean……. it's just sad…….a sad, sick person.’ 'Yeah.' I replied flatly, 'Boy!……..Hmmm.’ She then stared at me like she did during the meeting. 'Elijah. It was you?’ I feigned a laugh and acted as though it was a joke, 'Yeah. It was me. Who cooked that food girl? Taste real good.’ She smiled and shook her head and went her way. I knew that she suspected the culprit to be a female so I was off the hook. Some years later I am employed elsewhere and I encounter Summer on Facebook. After a brief chat I admitted to her that I was the food molesting culprit. She laughed and said she knew. I asked her how did she know. She said that she found out after the meeting that I had a bowl exactly like hers. She had put 1+1 together. I said, 'So that whole time you spoke to me after the meeting. You knew?’ She said yes. She was playing along with me to judge whether I tampered with her food by accident, as she suspected, or if one of her enemies made me do it……..that my dumb reaction to her comments had said it all. ‘……..It tasted really good though,' was all I could think of saying. Lesson learned: When you tamper with a co-worker's food by accident, it's a good idea to go tell them.

Name: Elijah Williamson
Question: Can you describe the smelliest person you have met?
Answer: Some months ago I was on the bus headed homewards. One of my pleasures in life is being able to read leisurely without any disturbance whilst on the typically quiet journey home on such bus. But alas, on that very day, such was not in the cards for me. Not by a longshot. The biggest chatterbox I know in existence happened to come into the bus and sat directly opposite me prodding me on the shoulder while I sat with headphones on attempting to read. I groaned but extended courtesy towards listening and engaging in some small talk about her workplace gossip, family gossip, how great her husband is, how she feels about bla bla bla. Nothing is wrong with all this except that she is one of those rare individuals who doesn't allow the talk to falter and prods you with a barrage of inane questions as though to ensure she has your complete attention. While trying to evade some rather nosy and trifling questions I got a whiff of of a scent that can only be described as startlingly ominous. I grimaced a bit and stared suspiciously at my acquaintance and nervously took a moderate whiff to determine if she was the culprit. Thankfully she wasn't. I was wondering if was just a fluke scent that drafted temporarily from the netherregion of some coarse individual who had left the bus but the scent happened to linger on for some seconds longer. I told myself the scent was gone. But alas, like a slap in the face the scent struck me again. It was even more powerful this time. Even through my facemask I could smell the scent, a scent that could only be described as something so offensive that it was beyond bestial. It smelt as though someone rubbed a sweaty, boozy armpit against my nose and then held my face upon the taint of some scoundrel who refused to bathe for weeks. 'Are you smelling that?’ I asked Madame Chatterbox and she stared at me with a rather dumb smile and replied, 'Smelling what?’ There was a pause and she continued with her monologue interspersed with trivial questionings. I began to get a headache. Someone in the back stank the high hell but I couldn't determine who was the culprit. There was a security officer, a middle aged woman and a sleeping old man in the back. None of them looked like the kind of person whose power of stench could bring the dead back to life. The scent came in waves; faintly menacing at its best, repugnant at its worst. So as not to retch I had to practice breathing through my mouth, but I felt nauseous knowing that I was sucking in that toxic air through my mouth and into my lungs. Madame Chatterbox continued on, despite the natural disaster that occured right in front of her nose. 'I'm so tired. I could just drop on my bed and sleep until next Monday. But I have to cook for my husband. You know how hard it is to cook every evening? You cook? I'm sure you probably go out and buy food every day. Lucky you.’ I didn't know what was worse. Having to endure that scent or having to endure Chatterbox's prying and passive aggressive vents disguised as small talk. Whatever poison was worse, the combination of the two was like a hellish torture. I was hoping at some bus stop, whomsoever was the culprit would hop off the bus. Hardly anyone ever went as far as the final stop. It would usually be just me and (unfortunately) Madame Chatterbox. At mid point the middle aged lady left the bus. At three quarter point the security guard hopped off. The only person left was the sleeping old man. Funny thing was, he didn't look like someone who would smell like a modern day torture instrument. He was relatively well dressed and ordinary looking. Another funny thing was I never saw him in the bus nor in the village before. He was a complete stranger. He lay snoring unwares as to the destruction that lay manifest under his arms and amidst his much unattended nether regions. I felt such a rage at his stink at some point I wanted to grab him by the collar, drag him to the front by the driver and demand that the driver smell him and agree to kick him out the bus. But alas such would not be the case. Mr. Smelly stayed with us the entire journey and Madame Chatterbox squawked the entire trip until I was rendered temporarily disabled by a pounding headache. When Mr. Smelly awoke and saw the final stop he bolted upright and shouted to the driver that he was on the wrong bus. He ran to the driver and begged that he remain on the bus to head back where it came from. The driver, finally getting a whiff of the scent, roared for the man to exit the bus immediately. While we exited the bus I could hear Mr. Smelly drunkenly complain that someone could have woken him up and told him he was on the wrong bus. He would've stoppped off much earlier and head back to the bus station. Hearing him say that and acknowledging the fact that all the torture was unnecessary, made me want to walk up to him and murder him. But alas such was not to happen.
